notes: SIX inventory rows and no more, because these are the items the page's own content justifies. The method and the SpeculationData container are separate items: the container has its own syntax, its own gating and its own member list, and the page documents it as the object the method returns. The four members are separate items too - distinct IDL declarations, distinct output content, and distinct lifecycle (only preloads has the explainer's used/unused resolution; only navigationDestinationURL has the navigate-event exposure condition) - so none of them may be merged into another. FOLDED, and the reason is the rule rather than economy: PreloadData, PreconnectData and SpeculationNavigationData are IDL-only type names whose entire developer-facing meaning is what each element of the corresponding array is, which the explainer already expresses inline; keeping them as rows would have meant pointing their cells at the collection row's fragments, which is the fragment-inheritance defect the campaign exists to catch. SpeculationNavigationType folds into navigations.type and SpeculationEagernessValue into navigations.eagerness for the same reason - each is used by nothing else. CrossOriginMode cannot be folded because it is genuinely SHARED (preloads[].crossorigin and preconnects[].crossorigin); it is not a member of the page's declared surface, so it is recorded here rather than as an out-of-scope entry, and its value space is documented in the page's IDL. The element fields of the folded types (as, crossorigin, earlyhint, origin, tags, type, url, used) ARE declared by the page's syntax region, so they are listed out of scope with rationales - a fold still has to ACCOUNT for what it folds, or the declared-surface check correctly reads it as an unaccounted member. inputs and errors are marked not-applicable across every row, and that is a judgement about the surface, not padding: the method takes no arguments, every member is a readonly attribute with no constructor anywhere, and nothing in the IDL or the explainer throws - when the feature is absent the member is simply missing, which is feature gating rather than an exception. Two example cells were the reason this unit paused: the explainer's single usage example destructures only preloads and navigations, so preconnects and navigationDestinationURL had no page fragment demonstrating them. The fix was to QUOTE the explainer's own response-shape block into the Examples section with attribution rather than invent an example - every member the contract inventories is now shown by the source's own words, which is rule 74's direction (quote rather than paraphrase) applied to an artefact gap. An accuracy correction rode with this contract, verified against ChromeStatus directly: the page described the origin trial as desktop-only, while the record carries Android and WebView stages on the same 150-155 window, and now also carries an Extend Origin Trial intent staged 2026-09-07 that would run the trial to desktop M158. The page now says desktop, Android and WebView, and records the extension as a REQUESTED INTENT rather than a granted endpoint, re-freezing its reading date - the dating hedge survives because the sources do not settle the outcome. Three sentences on the page are the page's own synthesis rather than source quotes (the header-delivered-preloads claim, 'unused preloads are the waste signal', and 'the metadata needed to judge which rules pay off'); they are not used as sourced evidence for any cell. The page's own hedges all stand: the provisional-status hedge on navigationDestinationURL is justified by the explainer's outstanding TODO about finalizing how to expose that URL, and the interim compatibility table is justified by the absence of a BCD entry.
